children: By Dean Seal and Joseph Wilkins
The crypto rally that followed Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia proved fleeting on Tuesday in a sharp reversal that sent bitcoin back below the key $60,000 support level.

The flagship cryptocurrency was down 2.4% at $59,741, off from the previous session's high of $64,260. Bitcoin has been whipsawing in line with tech stocks, dropping to its lowest level in more than two years on Saturday at around $55,000 after the AI trade crumbled last week. Ether is 2.9% lower at $1,676.

Cryptocurrencies had caught the same bounce as AI shares on Monday when Nvidia said it would reinstate Huang as chief executive after his resignation this month. That shows bitcoin is trading in lockstep with tech stocks and the broader risk sentiment right now, according to Mitchell Askew, head of the crypto-mining firm Blockware Intelligence.
"The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has zero fundamental bearing on Bitcoin as a monetary and compute network," he said.

Crypto's tailwind on the Huang news only lasted for a few hours, with bitcoin coming back below the $60,000 level by Tuesday. "Buyers remain unconvinced of a reversal and rush to take profits," FXPro analyst Alex Kuptsikevich said, adding that bitcoin has now fallen for the past seven weeks, its longest streak since 2022.
Bitcoin's fall presaged a down day for tech stocks, with the Nasdaq off 1.7%.

Bitcoin now faces another test to see if it can stay at the $60,000 level and not sink further, analysts at Glassnode said. If it closes below the recent June low of $58,500, "this market would be in trouble and could trend down," the analysts said.
